standard_prerequisites.use: Gives the acyclicity of the total tensor product with a K-flat complex.

core_obligations: Observe that the complex in question is simply the hom complex SheafHom^bullet(E^bullet, F^bullet), because boundedness of the strictly perfect complex E^bullet converts the products in the definition into direct sums (proof lines 11838-11842).

For an acyclic complex K^bullet, form the comparison map gamma from the total tensor product of K^bullet with the hom complex to the hom complex of E^bullet into the total tensor product (proof lines 11843-11852).

Use K-flatness of F^bullet to see that the target of gamma is acyclic, and reduce the lemma to the statement that gamma is a quasi-isomorphism, completing the argument up to line 11879 (proof lines 11853 onwards).
proof_roadmap: Identify the hom complex with the SheafHom complex.
Introduce the comparison map gamma for an acyclic test complex.
Use K-flatness on the target and reduce to the acyclicity of gamma.
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that in the situation computing R-Hom out of a strictly perfect complex, if the representing complex of the target is K-flat then the resulting hom complex is K-flat as well. The proof identifies the hom complex with the SheafHom complex because boundedness of the strictly perfect complex turns the products in the definition into direct sums, then for an acyclic complex K^bullet considers the comparison map gamma from the total tensor product of K^bullet with the hom complex to the hom complex of the strictly perfect complex into the total tensor product, notes that the target is acyclic by K-flatness of the second argument, and reduces to showing that gamma is a quasi-isomorphism (proof lines 11838-11879). H2: the identification of the hom complex and the reduction to the acyclicity of gamma are the substance.
